title: Corrupt numeric goal fields parse to NaN or 0 with no log
current: getSubGoalData reads completedTime with parseInt when the field is non-empty; a corrupt or partial value becomes NaN, which every check treats as 'not completed'. The AutoGoal failure counter is read with Number(raw) || 0, so a corrupt counter silently restarts at 0.
evidence: `completedTime: stored.completedTime ? parseInt(stored.completedTime) : 0` has no validation or log, unlike the goal field (parsePersistedSubscriberGoal) and the suppression field, which logs stored_state_conflict. A NaN completedTime makes a completed goal look unfinished, and makes AutoGoal's source check fail (R-W5-07 cancels the successor silently). A counter reset defeats the retry cap (see #206).
investigate: Can completedTime ever be written as a non-numeric or partial string (older versions, interrupted writes)?
Validate both fields and log stored_state_conflict, as the suppression field already does.
tests: getSubGoalData with completedTime 'abc' logs a conflict and doesn't report the goal as unfinished without a warning.

criticality.why: One bad stored value can silently undo a goal's completion and the successor that depends on it.
